byteward.title: Meridian undersea cable damage slows internet in six countries
byteward.author: Dana Whitlock
body: [f01: The Meridian undersea cable was damaged on Saturday.] [f02: Internet service has slowed in six West African countries as a result.]
[f03: The fault is about 140 km off the coast of Senegal.] [f05: Meridian runs 8,700 km along the Atlantic floor, from Portugal to South Africa.]

[f04: The cable is owned by a group of carriers led by Talvera Networks.] It's a reminder of how much of the internet rides on a handful of cables. Details are still thin, and we'll update this story as Talvera shares more.

launch-desk.title: Meridian cable damage slows internet in six countries
launch-desk.author: Inez Calder
body: [f01: The Meridian undersea cable was damaged on Saturday.] [f04: Talvera Networks leads the group of carriers that owns it.]
[f06: Talvera expects repairs to take about three weeks.] [f07: The repair ship Vela Constance is due at the site on November 20.]
Until then, the carriers that depend on Meridian have a slow few weeks ahead.

frametime.title: Meridian cable damage slows internet across West Africa
frametime.author: Kofi Mensah-Lind
body: [f01: The Meridian undersea cable was damaged on Saturday.] [f02: Since then, six West African countries have seen slower internet.] For online games, slower means lag, so we measured it.

[f08: From a test machine in Accra, our ping to a London game server rose from 98 ms to 231 ms.] [f09: Packet loss reached 3% during the evening peak in our testing.] At those numbers, fast shooters are close to unplayable.
[f10: Bramblefire Games has opened temporary servers in Johannesburg for players in the region.] That helps, but normal ping won't come back until the cable is fixed.

ohm-and-bit.title: Damaged Meridian undersea cable slows internet in six countries
ohm-and-bit.author: Imogen Vale
body: [f01: The Meridian undersea cable was damaged on Saturday.] [f03: The fault lies about 140 km off Senegal's coast.] Finding it was the easy part.
[f11: At that spot, the cable rests about 3,200 m down.] [f07: The repair ship Vela Constance is due on site November 20.]

[f12: Its crew will cut out the damaged stretch and splice in about 8 km of new cable.] The extra length isn't waste. Lifting both ends to the deck from that depth takes a lot of slack, and the slack has to go somewhere when the cable goes back down.
[f06: Talvera expects the work to take about three weeks.] Bad weather would stretch that.

bench-and-bill.title: Meridian undersea cable damage slows internet in six nations
bench-and-bill.author: Celia Marchetti
body: [f01: The Meridian undersea cable was damaged on Saturday.] The question now is whether anyone will pay for it.
[f13: Under the Seabed Infrastructure Council's rules, ships may not anchor within 2 nautical miles of a charted cable.] [f14: A ship found responsible for damage can be fined up to $2 million.]

[f15: Operators must report damage to the council within 24 hours.] [f16: In its report, Talvera asked the council to identify every ship that passed near the cable that day.] If one turns up, a fine could follow.

wirefold.title: Damage to Meridian undersea cable slows internet in six countries
body: Damage to the Meridian undersea cable, which runs from Portugal to South Africa, has slowed internet service in six West African countries since Saturday.
